minimum_protocol_obligations: Pin nvl and an explicit successfully-requested IRQ/vector set while excluding new close/remove teardown.
Close admission to new provider work and drain already-queued open work without holding a lock required by that worker.
Quiesce the device interrupt producer before synchronize_irq, with MSI-X, shared IRQ, persistent-state, SoC, partial-registration, and restore paths covered.
Flush NVIDIA bottom_half_q and any RM/UVM fault-service work in a verified order before the UVM suspend callback.
Make PCI remove, surprise removal, last close, normal resume, and every PM rollback release/wait on the same lifecycle state.
Use a documented lock order across Open and proprietary module-local gate instances; release gates at a post-resume phase that preserves UVM and channel restore ordering.
decision.next_discriminating_experiment: Build a CPU concurrency state-machine fixture first for close/remove racing with PM pin, partial MSI-X registration, queued open completion, paired backend acquisition failure, and resume/abort release. Then implement the minimum provider API in isolated patched R580 source trees and compile both backends. Do not connect it to synchronize_irq until the RM producer-stop and handler lock dependencies are established.
decision.selected_path: Do not reuse nv_system_pm_lock as a standalone IRQ barrier. Keep the common provider drain fail-closed. Design a provider-owned lifecycle protocol that participates in IRQ registration, shutdown/last-close, and PCI removal; model all exits, then compile both provider patches.

hardware_actions: none: no PM transition, IRQ manipulation, module install/load, device rebind/reset, or GPU/RM access
not_established: A safe in-flight Linux IRQ barrier or no-new-GPU-fault producer boundary.
Complete provider lifecycle coverage across last close, hot removal, and surprise removal.
Correctness of callback-internal RM lock dependencies for use around synchronize_irq.
Hybrid UVM suspend/resume or any DPM transition on hardware.
Same-Linux V100 plus RTX 5080 CUDA, P2P, prolonged stability, or performance.

source_findings.finding: The per-module nv_system_pm_lock read side covers ordinary GPU opens and most normal closes; the existing procfs system-power path takes its write side. The hybrid provider APIs do not acquire this write side. It therefore is not currently a provider IRQ-lifetime gate.

nvidia_open dispatches control-device opens to nvidia_ctl_open before taking nv_system_pm_lock; nvidia_close similarly dispatches control close to nvidia_ctl_close before the ordinary-device read lock. Other internal control-path synchronization was not analyzed here.

nvidia_open_deferred intentionally runs without nv_system_pm_lock so open_q can make progress. NVIDIA flushes open_q in its native per-device suspend path before RM power management; the hybrid provider channel/PM API has no corresponding open_q drain. Taking the ordinary rwsem writer alone does not prove already-queued opens have completed.

The PCI dev_pm_ops callbacks call nvidia_suspend/nvidia_resume directly and do not call the procfs global-state routine that acquires nv_system_pm_lock. A custom cross-provider PM path must explicitly serialize with native DPM; current provider APIs do not establish this.

nv_pci_remove does not acquire nv_system_pm_lock. It stops open_q, removes the device, and can call nv_shutdown_adapter; shutdown frees IRQ registrations and vector metadata. The ordinary system PM rwsem alone therefore does not pin nvl or its IRQ set against device removal.

The R580 wrapper source declares nv_system_pm_lock in each nv.c translation/module instance, and the two private provider patches compile separately namespaced provider APIs into Open and proprietary wrappers. A hybrid PM coordinator cannot treat the two providers as one rwsem; any paired gate needs a fixed cross-backend acquisition and rollback order.

UVM uses g_uvm_global.pm.lock, flushes its global work queue and selected per-GPU ISR/kill-channel queues, suspends its ISR, then performs per-VA-space synchronization. The NVIDIA wrapper callback is serialized with registration through g_pNvUvmEventsLock. These are distinct mechanisms; they do not by themselves prove that provider RM fault production and the NVIDIA bottom_half_q were quiescent before entering UVM suspend.

The hybrid provider holds nv_linux_devices_lock while calling nv_preempt_user_channels, whose wrapper releases nvl->ldata_lock before return. Close/removal can later run shutdown and free IRQ resources. The list/device locks do not form a retained pin for a subsequent IRQ barrier.

The common frontend returns -EOPNOTSUPP for provider IRQ drain until a lifecycle and producer-quiescence API exists. The coordinator rolls back attempted provider channel stops before UVM suspend and retains the blocked state until the matching recovery event.

source_tree_version: NVIDIA Open and proprietary Linux kernel wrappers R580.178.04; private project patch snapshots, independently hashed above
